An excellent dash cam, super high definition video quality, looks great, works great, love it so far!  With a 2.7’’ screen, it is great to see the camera recorded right away, it is very convenient for menu settings, adjustment and video playback, too.  After it’s installed on the windshield and plugged into the cigarette lighter, the camera will record automatically when I turn on the engine. It will automatically turn off when I switch the engine off.  This dash cam shoots really awesome video for both day and night! It records footage up to 1296P Super HD at 30fps, the highest video resolution I can find on Amazon. It can show clearly the license plate and other details in front of my car on the video. While it supports recording 1080P Full HD video at 60fps, technically shoots more images than that at 30fps, particularly fits for high-speed motion, but I cannot find obvious differences on the video.  GPS is very cool and it's showing my route and speed. There’s CD Player comes along with the dash cam, simply put it in my laptop, open the video player and drag a MOV file to it, Google map pops up with route and speed information. GPS also automatically sets the exact date and time to be displayed on videos, simply specify the desired time zone in the menu. Two thumbs up!  As is specified on the detail page, there’re four recording modes in the dash cam, and I tried them all. 1. Loop Recording: I insert a 64GB micro SD card in the dash cam and left it records in the car (with a hard wire kit provides continuous power), and check it the other day. The dash cam records about 8 hours all along, from the time showed on the video, the oldest clips were automatically replaced by new ones. The video clips were cut into average one minute segments on the micro SD card.  2. Emergency Recording: While the dash cam is recording, simply press the “M” key, the current video will be saved immediately and won’t be overwritten by loop mechanism. With a built in Gravity Sensor (G-sensor) the emergency recording mode will trigged automatically when it detects vibration around. This will be vital in an unpredictable incident, the video could be a critical evident in a traffic claim.  3. Motion Detection: A very useful feature, if an object passes in front of the vehicle, Dash Cam automatically starts detection and records motion. Without additional changes to setting, it can automatically detect and record a person approaching the parked car, whether to vandalize or steal from the car. You need to buy an additional hard wiring to provide continuous power.  4. Time Lapse Mode: A wonderful entertainment technique that records a scene or objects that has a slow state-of-change and turns it into a video that plays back in high speed. Have your camera stationary on something that changes slowly (e.g. plants growing) and start recording for hours or even days. Hours and hour’s worth of photos are compressed into a video with merely few minutes playtime, thus creating a time lapsing effect. It’s a pity that only 1sec/5sec/30sec for option in the menu.  On the video, there shows the real time, car plate, and driving speed, all can be set in the menu. Make sure you set the date and time correctly when you install your camera. This will be helpful when you have to offer competent evidence to avoid traffic claims.  While the dash cam is recording, short press the “Down” key, then the audio won’t be recorded; press the “Up” key, the screen will turn off and the cameras still keeps on recording, press the “Power” key, the IR LEDs will be activated. The shortcut keys have very corresponding icons showed clearly on the screen.  Thanks for the new generation mounting, the dash cam could be rotated 90 degree up and down, and when you push it to the topside, you can rotate it around, making it’s available to record inside and outside of your car.  The car charger seems high quality with a Blue LED and an extra USB port which can be used to charge my phone. Very Nice Design!  There’s HDMI cable in the package, but I still have not test it.  Con. 1. Expensive. Though coming with new features and better footage, the price is still a little  high for me. 2. Low capacity battery. I understand most dash cams are designed to work with car power supply, but camera with thus high tech. should have better battery, right? 3. Unspecified User Manual. There’re just basic instructions and operations, no further details.

It can also be set to lock your files if it detects a stop that generates the configured Grating - i.e. 1G. Since this has limited reviews here's mine. I bought this a few weeks ago and installed it into a CF Moto V3 replacing the stock radio/remote controls that it originally possessed my fitment is custom as I've built a replacement radio panel for it's install. the radio main unit mounts into the stock cf moto main radio location with a custom made bracket. The remote unit is mounted at an angle on the dash making easier use of the buttons.

Remote: The buttons are firm somewhat stiff in the key presses which is a good thing on a motorcycle as you don't want to accidently depress a button just putting your hand down on the unit (also good for a marine application as the buttons are fully resistant to water and silicon rubber covered. The rear of the remote is waterproof, If you mold fit the remote into your dash as I've done a good tip is to run a bead of silicon around the backside of the remote to fully seal it into the dash. Wire length from the remote is nice for a good run of wiring over 6' 6" in length give or take a few inches on the plus side. Uses a solid connector that comes capped in case you want to remove it and take the remote with you. the plastic doesn't feel cheap and I believe it's UV Stabilized as it hasn't faded yet in direct sunlight though is a tad hard to read in direct sunlight so mount it at an angle (I only get direct sunlight on the unit when the suns directly behind me.) If you want to correct this get a glare protector screen cover for a cellphone and put it on it'll make it readable in direct sunlight then (did this, it works excellently for me).

Radio main unit: The reception is good utilizing my bikes stock antenna which is an automotive type connector. In my unit i've got a voltage power stabilizer in line to the unit because of line noise from the stator *alternator (a boat probably wouldn't have this issue but my installation's unique so i have that issue). It's rather solidly built with good quality ABS plastic, (possibly stabilized but not sure on that) all the connectors have cap ends to keep water out except for obviously the wiring harness, and the antenna connector. The connectors all feel solidly fitted to the wire ends. the rear of the radio has a solid heat sink installed with full rubber pass through fittings that are water resistant but not waterproof (you can fix that by adding rubber silicon to where the wires connect but that's not really needed if mounted up inside of an enclosure or behind a dashboard), As for station reach it's actually VERY GOOD I'm getting stations from beaumont and port arthur on am and a few fm stations from those areas, I live in the houston area (with bikes stock antenna, may upgrade that later though). Station lock is excellent and it Does remember the last station you were on (including presets) even when disconnected from power for long periods of time. Winter time here so the bikes battery was removed for 2 weeks before being reconnected for installation of a standalone dvr system with separate camera's radio went right to the last station i had on.

Installation: For me was rather quick with the included wiring harness that comes with the unit and added some quality quick connectors to hook it all together. All of the wires are labelled making installation a snap I don't have pictures of the installation on my bike my camera's broken atm but I am including pictures of the unit itself (prior to install) so you can see how it looks with the wiring unlike the stock picture of it on the description. The fade seen on the screen is from the screen protector film on it that the factory sticks on it, so it's not broken or scratched just got the film on it still.

Ipod added on: If you intend to use the Ipod connection be expected to purchase separately an adaptor connector called a MIL-IPlug to connect it with.
USB: It Does read MP3 files on usb sticks, don't expect much from it though, it'll play files not play lists! So if you make a ton of play lists and expect this to play the files linked with those play lists and it doesn't work I did warn you!

The FM tuner seems a little on the weak side but it has settings I haven't played with yet. The one AM station i listen to barely came in.

It's also much better looking than last years model both in layout and lighting. The dimmer keeps it from being obnoxious. I don't use the light effects except for when the phone rings. The fact that you can fine tune the lighting effects was a big selling point for me.

Bluetooth audio and phone conversations are perfect. I mounted the mic on my steering column. iPhone synced easily and reconnects when i turn the car on. Seems to be efficient with power compared to other bluetooth systems I've used. All contacts and track titles load on to the deck so when someone calls you know who it is.

No complaints so far. Some complain about it being too dim or too bright. Have you people had an aftermarket deck? it's always been an issue. I had a Clarion deck in my previous car, and I had to put electrical tape over the screen because it was blinding at night. Seriously, dangerous. The dimmer button gives you several brightness settings to match the situation. I keep mine turned down all the way and keep it green to match the Subaru's interior lights, and I can actually see it better in the day time than the factory unit.

I bought a 32gig USB stick, one of the tiny Sandisc ones, to pair with the deck. I plan to format it in FAT32 and load a big chunk of my library and have it dedicated for the car. This will save iPhone battery for music and probably marginally increase audio quality. I'll update the review with that info.

UPDATE: I went on a 10 hour road trip with the unit over the weekend and installed the 'SanDisk Cruzer Fit CZ33 32GB USB Flash Drive.'

The flash drive in the USB slot worked great. Very good quality and the interface for finding music is decent enough. I just made sure I was orderly with the files and deleted 'The' from the names of bands. It plays continuously and picks up where you left off when you get back in the car. It was a pain to get the music on the drive in an orderly way . A lot of my older files were apple AAC (which isn't supported) so i had to manually convert to mp3 and there was a loss of quality there. Other than that, though, I'm glad i got it done. having a 32 gig dedicated flash drive for the unit is awesome.

On the road, I did notice a problem with glare. Some people said the unit is too dim for bright daytime settings, but that's not the case. It's that the screenis too glossy in the plastic and it constantly reflects. I will probably trim an iphone anti-glare screen protector for this issue. Overall, though, it didn't bother me much.

Siri worked great on the road with the unit. Calls were clear and I checked NFL scores since I had to drive on a Sunday. When playing music through USB, the unit switches to the phone and back automatically for calls and Siri.

***A BIG However, if you use iPhone navigation, you have to use Bluetooth Audio for the directions to come through the car. This means that if you want that seamless fade out of the music for Siri to tell you where to go, you have to run BTA and NAV at the same time, which means your battery will last about 5 minutes in the phone. I don't fault the deck though, I'm sure it's an iPhone software thing.

Driving at midnight in the middle of nowhere in pitch darkness, the unit was still too bright even on the lowest setting. It wasn't blinding like other decks I've had, but I wish i could have turned it down a little bit more. Or, if it could be wired into the car's OEM dimmer wire that would be nice.

Overall, I'm very happy. Never had better sound on a road trip.

A bow and hearty congratulations fo Audio Technica for respecting the serious music listener where it matters most, true value!

Got a set of these speakers about two years ago and a second set about 6 months after the first. The fact that I got a second set should suggest how good these speakers are. I've trusted the Kenwood brand ever since my folks bought a Kenwood component system way back in 1982 (thanks mom and dad for introducing me to this awesome brand). Years after, I decided to take possession of it seeing how they were in the market for a newer (smaller) system. That system is still in my living room albeit the years (and the hands of a certain youngling) have taken a toll on some of its functionality. One thing that hasn't changed though is the quality of the sound it produces. That tradition carries on with the Kenwood KFC-1689ie speakers as they have superb sound reproduction. The specs for these babies are terrific and I would say they are the best value you are gonna likely find at 2-50 watts RMS and 200 watts peak power. Most speakers have 40 watts RMS tops, and even at a higher price range, the peak power tends to be a crappy 100 watts or 150 tops. Brands like Alpine, Clarion and Infinity although terrific too, are not the best of values as the specs tend to be quite low and the prices quite high. The important thing is not how high they would go though, but instead how good will they sound at the higher levels (and the lower ones for that matter) and these speakers won't dissapoint. The highs and mids are sharp and clear, and the bass... oh, the bass has to be the star of this show. I would say the thumping produced by these speakers might be equivalent to having an 8-inch subwoofer installed. It is robust to say the least. Of course it also has a lot to do with the kind of music you listen to (I listen to black/nordic/gothic metal mostly, but I also listen to some other genres) and (most importantly in this era of CD-Rs and MP3s) the quality of the recordings.
In my case they are powered by a Kenwood KDC-205 receiver with a Mosfet 50x4 watts (22x4 RMS) spec and I gotta say that they feel underpowered even with that, meaning that they can take so much more. My initial setting had an old Audiovox equalizer/amplifier, that added an extra 50 watts to the equation and that whole setting produced the sweetest sounding music I have ever laid my errr... ears on. Unfortunately I had to uninstall that equalizer/amplifier because it was incompatible with the receiver (and to pretty much any current receiver) as it triggered some sort of protection feature that receivers nowadays possess. Equalizer/amplifiers are no longer being made apparently, it is either one or the other but not both in a single unit, so I am left to reminisce about what was. Maybe one if these days I'll try an amplifier, if you have the space and the money, I would recommend getting an amplifier right away.
As far as the looks (and even without taking into account that they match my car's interior), these speakers are very nice looking, arguably the best looking speakers out there. The construction is quite sturdy and thankfully I have not had any trouble with them for as far as I have had them installed. Asides from a bit of dust that has collected, I would say they look as good as they did when they came out of the box, no melted rubber, no warping, no color fading, etc.
Finally, if you are reading this review it means that you are doing some research before buying, so I got to say when I bought this pair I was actually looking for the Kenwood 1789ie, which are 7-inch speakers with an RMS that goes to 55, and peak that goes to 220 if I remember correctly. No stores were selling them at the time though, some only listed them as \\"coming soon\\", while others as \\"out of stock\\", the point is that I finally settled on these because of that. When I bought the second pair I had a chance to compare the 1689s vs the 1789s at a local Best Buy. I was gonna buy the 1689s regardless because I wanted the specs to match the ones I had, but still, I wanted to compare them. After listening to both sets I was glad that I went with the 1689s in the first place. Both sound awesome, it is just that the 1689s' bass response sounds more robust than the 1789s for some reason, whereas the 1789s place more emphasis on highs and mids (the comparison was done using the same receiver without changing any settings when switching between speakers). I guess, which set is better is a matter of personal preferences. Back then no other set of speakers came close to matching the specs of either of these, at any price.
All in all, I say Kenwood rules!!

I purchased this product about a year ago, and can say I am quite happy with it.  It took my 2004 Honday Odyssey minivan from 20 mpg on the highway to 38 mpg.  The size is perfect to fit inside the engine area, but I chose to put it between the front bumper and the front left wheel well.  Have been using Potassium Hydroxide as my electrolyte, and have had no corrosion from the unit.  I dis-assembled it once to clean it, and was satisfied that the stainless steel plates were not breaking down.  The vendor was able to put together a unit that had more plates in it than my home-made 13-plate unit, and takes up less space.  While there are skeptics to trying this, I have found the biggest obstacle is not leaking the hydrogen out somewhere.  Being the smallest element in the table, if there is a crack somewhere, hydrogen will fit through the smallest when no other element may.  My biggest success came when I stopped using black rubber gas tubing.  It may be fine for gasoline, but I suspect it was poreous enough that the hydrogen was being abosrbed into it.  I use re-inforce plastic in some places, copper tubing in others.  Since there are few ways to test for the presence of hydrogen leaks (a match or filling a baloon and see if it floates), had to come up with a good but safe way to test for it making it out the tubing to the air intake.  Nice design, good product as far as HHO generators go.

I was intrigued by this item, thought I would give it a try. I thought I would mount it between two pieces of plexi glass and stick it on a shelf between some bookshelf speakers. I'll not be putting it in my car window, but you sure could, if you wanted to. I gave a top rating because I do like it, but it is not perfect. For $15 it really is an amazing bit of technology. The Sticker part is about as thick as 3 sheets of paper, very thin. The cold sheet lights, or whatever they call them, are very bright and vibrant. I would even say they are brighter than LED's, and they basically have no thickness. Its like they are printed on the plastic sheet. The black box contains no batteries. I had to open it up and take a peek because the power cord is referred to as a charger. There is a circuit board in there with about as much stuff on it as a solid state radio or amplifier. It is a very clever device. I had a power (brick) laying around that puts out 12 volts and about 1 amp, and the plug actually fit, so I just plugged it in to that.
There are two things that are not great with this thing, maybe a deal breaker for some. The first would be that the microphone or sensor that triggers the light show is not very sensitive. I am listening to music quite loud, and its not picking up much. I moved the black box right in front of the speaker and cranked the sensitivity up (there is a knob for that) and its full on, full off, not really very accurate. If I hold it about six inches away from the speaker, playing pretty loud, and turn the sensitivity down a bit it is best. I think I may actually try putting it inside of a speaker someday. The other thing is that this is not really a true spectrum analyzer, it's a cool light show that emulates one. When a song is in a heavy bass beat, it lights up randomly across the full spectrum. I have yet to mount it on plexi glass, but I will. I am just using it as a decoration, a live poster if you will.

It needed to be "normally open" which refers to the switch - the magnet holds the switch open, and when the door opens the sensor separates from the magnet and closes.  The transmitter comes set defaulted for normally open, so I had to put the jumper back in, and it worked fine.  The second one I use on a garage door about 40' away and through a brick wall.  I bought a garage door sensor from another vendor and hooked that up.  It's a wide gap sensor (up to 2.75") and works also as normally open.  The transmitter has no problems transmitting that distance through the brick wall.  Very pleased with both units.  Also glad they use 9v batteries (1 each).  Had a cheapo door sensor that used an odd battery that was hard to find.

Even if I were a forgetful person, this perceptive feature allows the dash cam to do its work superbly without any initial user interaction. As my friends and I traveled, mile by mile and state by state, the dash cam recorded everything. The beautiful lightning storms that lit up the Nevada desert skies? Recorded to be re-watched anytime we want. The bison and elk roaming in front of our car at the national park? We will be able to watch these majestic creatures on my HDTV using the supplied HDMI cable. And that one aggressive driver who was talking on his mobile phone while driving, and decided to honk at us? Yeah, we have evidence of that, too.  On the second night of the road trip, while my friend was driving and all of us were asleep, we were jolted awake by sudden braking. She claimed that an animal had sprinted in front of the car and she had to hit the brakes. We thought she was perhaps imagining things, but thanks to the IR LED night vision of this dash cam, along with the ability to instantly play back recording directly on the dash cam's 2.7'' HD wide-screen LCD after we pulled over to the side of the road, it was verified that a deer was in the headlights. The hard plastic and metal construction gives the product an air of durability, and the swivel-suction mount attaches securely and easily, and when needed, detaches cleanly.  Although our magical summer vacation has sadly come to an end, this dash cam is still useful, every day. As I cruise around town, I allow the dash cam to record. I went looking for a Bluetooth speaker to pair with both my iPhone and Laptop to improve my experience listening to internet radio and came across this new offering from Tech-Life. The BeatBlock matches what I was looking for exactly with good volume and long battery life - after first charging it the unit lasted about a week of \\"normal\\" use consisting of about 1-2 hrs a day of mid volume listening (your mileage may vary)...

I like the rectangular design and sturdy construction and it was very easy to pair with both my devices. Charging was easy either from the laptop or any generic 1 Amp USB charger using the provided USB to micro USB cable or direct micro-usb charger if you already have one - more companies should standardize on this for a charging port so that we can reduce the bucket-full-of-chargers that I have to maintain for all my tech gadgets!

Two minor issues with the product - neither of which changed my mind about liking the unit (more about this later) - (1) as someone else commented, button push feedback beeps can be very loud, even when the unit volume is low; (2) the background noise when no signal is present is a bit louder than I would have liked, which can be a common issue with Bluetooth devices, however this becomes unnoticeable when any reasonable signal volume is being listened to.

Back on the subject of liking the unit - I was trying to decide if the background noise was significant enough of an issue to stop me from keeping the unit and contacted Tech-Life's customer support on the issue. This was initially difficult to do as it can't be found in their included documentation, but can be found on their limited web site. However once contact was made I found them to be extremely helpful and supportive in answering my questions and even getting me a 2nd unit to try out for an A-B comparison. I wish more customer/technical support organizations were this responsive!

I ended up deciding to keep the unit as all the things I like about the BeatBlock (design, battery life, volume, ease-of-use) far outweighed the two negatives I reported above.

I have come to trust the SONY name over the years so when it came time to splurge for a Reader, I decided to give their product a try.  While it may not contain every feature on your wish list, it is quite a remarkable device and quite satisfactory in this phase of the eBook Reader evolutionary process.    While I do enjoy the occasional novel, my primary purpose in purchasing the device was to permit me to have ready access to reference materials and documents useful in my profession as an attorney.  With the ease of loading pdf, WORD, RTF, txt, epub, and easily-converted other formats, It has exceeded my expectations.  I have Adobe Acrobat Professional which me to create my own documents in pdf format quite easily and I have been quite impressed with the reader's handling of them.  Dual-column documents can be viewed in either portrait or landscape and when the font size is increased through the reader's menu, it seamlessly pages down one column and then the other.  Embedded links within the pdf are still functional, allowing me to navigate easily on the Reader.    The memory chip slots on the device permit me to easily transport many many gig of documents with the device.  Whether accessing a document from the inserted memory card or from the on-board memory, the access is quick and smooth.    Using the Reader Library software available from SONY free-of-charge, makes managing documents a breeze.  I have yet to consult the manual, finding the operation of the software and the Reader to be quite intuitive.    Battery life is another plus, in as it seems to go forever between charges.  Charging while connected to the computer through the USB means that the optional wall charger is an unnecessary luxury.    Probably the key selling point on this particular SONY Reader is the ability to highlight, underline, and add hand-written or typed notes to documents.  This permits me to annotate documents quickly and easily while away from a computer.  I cannot imagine a reader without this capability being very useful for me.    The MP3 player is a nice extra which permits me to listen to music, audio books, or anything else in MP3 format while in the car.  I connect the stereo jack to the Reader and to the input jack on my car stereo.  It is just an extra tossed in that is really not central to the Reader's function.    Documents and files cannot only be annotated but also deleted from the device without a computer connection.  This is handy when you find duplicate documents or unwanted materials on the Reader.    I imagine that as Readers evolve, there will be backlight, color, and more in the future, but for now I am more than satisfied with the product.  The complaints about screen glare seem a bit rediculious to me since anything with a plastic surface is subject to some glare when at the proper angle.  A simple adjustment of the angle and any glare is gone.  The ability to increase font size on the Reader for individual documents more than compensates for any difficulties in reading the text.    While the latest Sony reader, which costs a bit more, does include wireless access to the book store, I do not find this valuable to me at this time.  I am at the computer each day and adding a downloaded document to the reader takes only a few seconds and keeps the battery topped up on the Reader.    I find that many retailers permit you to try the product for 14 days and if not satisfied return for a full refund.  Given that option, there is nothing to lose in giving this model a try.  I did and was sold almost instantly.    This device should provide you with a solid dependable reader until the next generation entices you to upgrade.

I bought this charger for my battery-sucking DROIDX before a 20 hour flight followed by 5 weeks in a place with infrequent chances for contact with an electrical outlet. It was perfect - the very best item I bought for my trip - and more than worth the price.

The outer case is very basic and you have to read the manual to figure out what the single light display blinking patterns mean, but the simplicity means there's little to go wrong or break on the outside. I like it. It has a single button, and you push that button when you've plugged in your phone or tablet and want it to charge. That's it - simple. The only flaw in the simple system is that when you have your phone charging on it, all the lights go off and sometimes at a quick glance I forget whether it's charging or switched off and have to check the phone itself. Not a big deal, but it would be nice to have a tiny indicator that says whether it's actively charging or switched off.

As far as charging the charger itself, you plug it into a wall and it charges really quickly. Overseas with my power converter it charged fully in an hour and possibly less. In the US it takes 2 hours or a bit more to charge it from near empty. Once charged, it can charge my DROIDX about 4 full times and still have some juice left in it (probably can go up to 5 charges, but I've never needed to). It also charges the phone battery faster than a wall outlet does. And the unit turns itself off once the phone is fully charged, which is also great.

It comes with a weirdly short cord I've never used - I have a kabillion charging cords that fit it (micro USB to USB) so I just use one of my extras for it.

I don't know what I would have done without it while traveling. I even loaned it out on the plane and between my several phone charges and their phone charge, the external battery was still at half capacity when I arrived. I now carry it with me in the car and in my bag and don't bother hunting for an outlet when I go places. I can plug my phone in, start the charger going, throw both things in my purse and it charges while I'm walking around. I love it. It was a great purchase.

I have used many, many different MP3 players for swimming. I swim one mile a day and could not get through the boring cadence without the help of music and I have found that these ear buds do an excellent job. I have found that the biggest weakness for any underwater MP3 players are the ear pieces. If you are kicking against a wall when making that reverse very few ear buds can take that pressure.

The H20 Surge mini are excellent but pricey, but they at least dropped the price about $20 from what it used to be. But it's an investment and does the job. You may want to look at the Aerb 4G Waterproof MP3 (non screen) player as well, it almost as cheap as these ear buds and makes for an excellent swimming experience when paired with these ear buds. I have reviewed that product as well. Also will allow you to feel less guilty about the money spent on these ear buds since the player is so cheap.

The only con on this product is the length of the cord. They seem to assume swimmers place this on their waist which would be very difficult to swim with if that was the case. So in short, if you attach it to the back of your goggles like I do, then you have to wrap the massive amount of cord unto a three inch stiff connector sticking straight up out of an MP3 playe. My advice is to wrap the cord around the connector at the top. Use a bread bag tie thingy and wrap it securely. Don't use a rubber band as the pool water rots if fairly quick. You can also wrap the wire around the goggle bands as well. Despite this nit, I still recommend this product wholeheartedly. A couple of key items to remember when using these:

1. Start with the larger ear bud rubber ends first then work your way down to the smaller sizes if that doesn't fit. If you use the larger sizes, you get a tighter barrier against the water.

2. You should consider wetting the ear buds lightly in the water before you place them in your ear, it seems to keep them more secure in your ear for some reason.

3. When you insert them in your ear pull back the top of your ear with your opposite hand, that will stretch it and allow the ear canal to gently wrap more snugly around the ear bud.

It is rare when the water enters the ear canal if you take these three steps you can enjoy the music much and swim much better. Once water gets in your ear you are hosed for the rest of the swim and that goes for any ear piece. Happy swimming!

I can't recommend the Cube highly enough.

Operation:

Setting the current date:

Save and protect an important recording:

This is an important button so you need to remember where it is situated. This will save and protect that segment from being overwritten when the camera does its loop recording. Then automatically the camera will protect that particular recording segment when it sense an impact. It is important to have this on because on a typical crash you may forget out of confusion to press the SOS button to save it. Or you may be unconscious to do so. G sensor's sensitivity can be adjusted. Test its sensitivity for your preferred setting. Too much sensitivity will protect your video even on sudden breaking.

I've only seen one other review for this unit (which can be alternately branded under the "Nippon" or "Audiopipe" names), but I figured I'd give it a shot. I wasn't expecting much, but having 9 bands of EQ for this price was alluring and I bit. The build quality is good. Nothing seems loose, connections are solid and remain tight on the variety of RCA connections I tried. The power plug connector holds firmly in place (on a side note: the power connector is tossed in with the mounting hardware in the packaging, and is easy to overlook when you first open it up). One feature I REALLY appreciate is a locking center detent on all of the EQ adjustments and the fader, as this lets you know when you've centered a band back to null without having to guess. The blue backlighting is bright but evenly spaced, so there's not one huge bright spot behind a few knobs and none on others. The control knobs seem firm and smooth, with no slop during adjustment. Measuring the response with an RTA, all bands seem to be accurately labeled within about 10% of an octave (as an example: the 1khz band seems to be centered at 1.1khz, or 1/10 octave above it's rated frequency. This is not a problem at all and is a very minor error). The filters are relatively high-Q and don't overlap which in my opinion is a good thing. I measured a 10dB cut with each filter all the way down, and a ~12dB boost with it up. I don't have access to an oscilloscope, so clipping could not be measured, but from a subjective point-of-view the signal sounds very clean. When I first connected the unit, I used a switched 12v+ lead for both the switched and constant 12v+ terminals on the power plug and experienced significant turn-on "pop". Wiring the power plug correctly with both a switched and constant 12v+ lead eliminated the issue, and using a zero-bit track I haven't noticed any rise in noise floor, even with the unit level at its highest setting. To sum it up: I highly recommend this unit.

Background:
I'm a an engineer and a HAM operator.

My thoughts on this product:
You may notice that *all* of the crystal radio kits on Amazon have pretty poor reviewer ratings. I would like to point out that with even the best-conceived crystal radio, you may simply live in too poor a reception area for the AM stations the radio will be sensitive too. Being close to an FM radio tower will do no good at all. A crystal radio is powered *by* the radio energy, and is only sensitive to AM signals. If you can't tune anything you might need a much longer (and/or higher) wire as the antenna.

If you don't know if the radio is wired incorrectly or you simply aren't getting reception from a broadcast station, you should *at least* be able to hear crackling and static when touching the connections and the antenna wire, as well as noise from lightning during a storm. If the earpiece is *completely* silent, then revisit the wiring.

Regarding this kit specifically, the components are as good as I personally could have expected for the price. I really bought this just to have a demonstrator on-hand because it's a cheap way to get all the parts one needs in one package. The electrical "connectors" are funny but there's something to be said for including around-the-house parts.

The manual:
It could use more illustrations of the connections for sure, but I found the wording and drawings to be irresistibly charming if not optimistic. The product has clearly been changed slightly since the manual was written but no biggies; In general one just needs to have the common sense to realize when something has been done for you (pre-stripped wires, etc).

Tip: Finding a good ground connection can make all the difference in the world, and using your home's cold-water plumbing isn't a sure thing, especially if you're in a multi-story building and the plumbing is running in the walls around and above you, which will have the effect of negating the antenna. You may want to actually go outside and run the ground wire to a big metal stake of some kind that's actually stuck in the ground, especially if the soil is moist in your area. This will be more difficult in a desert-climate.

Final thoughts:
-This IS a science project after all and one shouldn't necessarily feel that the kit is inadequate if experimentation is required to make it work.

I know that McDonald's slogan sounds really cheesy, but it is so true for my iAUDIO4. I have literally fallen in love with it and I don't go anywhere without it.
Let me explain to you why I love this device so much:
First of all the accessories that come with your iAUDIO; it's all there: Your armband for sports, the carrying case, the headphones, line in cable, battery, manual, portable USB port and the USB cable. Admittedly, this doesn't make a great player, but it helps.
The body of the i4 is amazingly small and nearly completely made of lightweight aluminium. It feels and looks extremely durable. The unit is basically built around the iAUDIO's massive screen. Its 4 line LCD display is the biggest yet on any flash based mp3 player around. The screen also has 124 different backlight colours to choose from that give perfect readability in the dark. In direct sunlight, even though the backlight colours are no longer visible, the display is easy to read.
Sometimes I wonder how Cowon managed to fit all the following features into the iAUDIO's little body: line-in recording, voice recording, FM radio, FM radio recording & an mp3, wav, wma player. Even though the recording functions are all limited to a maximum of 128 kbps mp3s they all function well and have excellent sound on playback. The FM radio receiver is extremely powerful and can receive a lot of stations, although I live in the middle of nowhere.
Concerning the most important aspect of any audio player: The iAUDIOs sound can only be described as being extremely good. It's clean as hell and has more body than e.g. the iriver 700 or 800 series. The equaliser is also awesome (5 band; each band has +/-28) and the BBE is great! Altogether there are over 1.6 Trillion possibilities of setting the iAUDIOs jetEffect settings. That should do for pretty well everyone ;-)
Uploading songs to your player is easy. Just connect it to your PC and it will automatically register as a removable storage device (it shows up under "my computer"). Now all you need to do is drag'n'drop your songs and you are ready to go.
Navigating on the iAUDIO is simple. It takes a bit of getting used to, but should be no problem for non-techy people. If there is something you really don't understand you can just consult the manual.
Battery life on the iAUDIO is not outstanding, but for AAAs it's good. I get a little more than 9 hours from my Sanyo 800 mAh batteries and 12-13 from alkalines.
So I have been praising the iAUDIO all the time, but there are also some minor negative points: There is a slight gap between 2 songs (find me a flash mp3 player that has gapless playback :-p ). The device only operates on USB 1.1 and not on USB 2. Transfer rates for the iAUDIO are roughly 0.75 MB/s which is fully utilizing the USB 1.1 standards. Don't let yourself be fooled by false advertising of USB 2 being up to 40 times faster for flash players. To date the fastest USB 2 transfer rate on flash players is 2-3 times faster than the iAUDIOs USB 1.1.
The headphones that come packaged with the device can be too big for some peoples ears so you might have to buy some new ones. Also people with really big hands (I'm talking massive here) might have problems operating the iAUDIO4, because its controls are slightly on the small side.
The bottom line:
The iAUDIO4 is a good looking, tiny, really high quality device with excellent sound. Don't let yourself be put off by its trivial faults. The iAUDIO is awesome and I am sure you will love it too.

This is a sexy speaker. It sounds pretty good at low to moderate level. It is easy to pair with a Bluetooth device.

Why is this sexy? There is this garnet red LED underneath the top panel that fades in and out, making this thing glow with a subtle gentle red light. The top has a faint Bluetooth logo that fades in and out. The glossy white body is sleek and gorgeous. So yes I like the way this speaker looks.

This is a mono speaker. The driver is a nice Mylar cone with a hefty rubber surround. The design is an enclosed cabinet - no vent. The top portion tries to spread sound out over a larger area. The speaker sounds best within about 20 degrees up and down from the opening. Detail falls off much higher or lower than that.

This is a talking speaker, this one is somewhat funny. Flip the switch on the bottom to power up the speaker and it says in an Asian female voice, "Power On". If the speaker hasn't been paired before or your Bluetooth is off, it says "Reaching for pairing." Once the speaker is paired it says "Connected."

Pairing is simple. Turn on the speaker; wait for it to say Reaching for pairing and the Bluetooth icon flashes quickly. On your device, turn on Bluetooth and look for FENDA Swan. Touch that line and after a few seconds the two will pair. On an iPhone the speaker charge level is displayed beside the Bluetooth icon.

The speaker can control volume and tracks. It can be used as a speakerphone. When there is an incoming call, the music stops. Touching the Bluetooth light answers the phone. Volume isn't great; you wouldn't use this in a conference room for a bunch of people. For one or two people in a small room it will work just fine.

I like the sound at low to middle volume. This is a perfect office, hotel room, or living room speaker - more of a personal speaker than room filler. At higher volume the whole thing gets strained and the music isn't very pleasant. With that in mind, this is a really nice speaker.

The Bluetooth range is surprisingly good. Most speakers this size quit working about 6 feet away. I was able to keep good clean connection at 20 feet. That's impressive. Don't get too excited though - you really can't leave the room and expect to stay connected.

The next time you use this speaker after it has been paired is very easy. Simply make sure Bluetooth is enabled on your device. Turn on the speaker power and the two will pair automatically.

The speaker charges via a microUSB cable (provided) - you will need to provide a computer USB port, an AC adapter, or a powerbank battery. There is no auxiliary 3.5mm audio jack - Bluetooth is the only way this speaker connects.

Here is another great product I discovered to use with my Note 2. This particular unit has a very portable footprint and it's relative slim with dimension of 119mm x 74mm x 18mm (4.7\\" x 2.9\\" x 0.7\\"). It's also pretty lightweight for 7000 mAh capacity, at 6.8 oz (193 g). It's definitely very comfortable and pocket/purse friendly. As a matter of fact, this unit is actually intended to be used on the go where you don't even have to worry about power cables since it has built in full usb cable for Input charging (a fast 5V, 1A port) and also micro-usb cable for one of the Output charging ports (5V, 1A). In addition to 1A output port with micro-usb cable, it also provides 2 additional usb ports with 2.1A and 1A outputs. These got you covered for any smart phone or tablet, and can also charge two devices at the same time.

For convenience if input charging cable is not long enough for you, New Trent also included USB extension chord which I found to be a great bonus. No other chords or adapters were included with this product. The device itself is very slick with a footprint reminding me a small external hard drive. The bottom of this power bank is finished matte while the top has a shiny piano finish. On the top you also have a discretely placed power button and 4 led power meter indicators with cool green lights. Those 4 lights partition power reading into 25% increments.

Beside its portability and convenience of built in cables, the main attraction of this device is a whooping 7000 mAh capacity. This is some serious number!!! And NT70T has this 7000 mAh speced at 3.7V - the voltage of the actual lithium battery. To be honest, I was a little skeptical at first because external battery market is flooded with a lot of high capacity external batteries that have exaggerated labels. So right away I put this battery to the test. I had my Note 2 discharged down to 25% while NT70T was charged all the way to full (4 leds lit up). I used 2.1A output port fora faster charging and used my own usb-to-micro-usb cable. My Note 2 battery got charged up to 100% in under 3 hours. That was very impressive. After charging it up, I checked with NT70T and it still had 3 leds on!!!! Of course, 3 leds doesn't mean it's at full 75% charge, but rather between 50% and 75% charge. But still, very impressive considering we are talking about our GN2 with 3100 mAh stock battery. As a bonus, you can actually charge your phone while charging NT70T, pretty cool although not recommended by manufacturer since it can accelerate aging of the battery.

In my opinion this is one of the top small footprint portable external battery chargers that offers simultaneous charging of two devices at the same time with one port being 2.1A and others at 1A, and having a whooping true 7000 mAh capacity!!! A must have if you need a portable backup battery and don't wont to part with your current smart phone case (to accommodate bulky extended battery). I definitely recommend NT70T EasyPack!

Also comes with a screen protector for the Ipod. Comes with great instructions that are easy to follow to adjust armband, put on screen protector, & lace up shoe pouch. I have not had any problems with my Nike+ finding/reading my transmitter in my shoe or the accuracy but I'm not someone that  takes my distance too seriously. (You do need to calibrate your Nike+ (instructions on Nike website) to make it more accurate.) Works fine for my weekly 5k runs!    Cons- The pouch has to be laced into the shoe which is somewhat time consuming so not good if you want to quickly remove the shoe pouch or wear your running shoes without the pouch on it a lot. (It is easy to remove the transmitter chip inside however- since it just velcros closed.) Also the pouch is not water-proof. As for the Ipod holder on the armband- the silicone Ipod holder part seems like it could tear easily if you are not careful inserting & removing your Ipod. Includes instructions that explains how to avoid that. (I wouldn't recommend this product if you won't be keeping your Ipod in the silicone skin most the time for that reason.) The screen protector was not really exciting for me but I guess it's a nice added bonus.     Overall these are great quality products for the price & I don't run without them!

It charges my Samsung Galaxy Tab Plus from 50% to full charge in 2 hours and 15 minutes, and I can get two charges to my Tab with it. It will charge my Galaxy Tab, my cell phone, and my Phillips Mp3 player together, and I can use my tablet as it charges if I want to.

This is the thing that really impressed me though...I charged the device to 100% four days ago, and haven't used it since. Before I wrote this review, I was curious how much it might have discharged in four days. When I connected it to my laptop USB, I still had four solid green bars! No noticeable discharge at all!

I am impressed with the New Trent products, and their customer service is the best I ever dealt with. I highly recommend the NT70T. It really is darn near perfect.

I use this device to transmit a DirecTV satellite receiver output to my earbuds (plugged into a cheap $24.00 Bluetooth audio adapater from Wally World), about 15' across the room. The manual says to keep the transmitter within 5 feet of the receiving device, which, if that were the case, I would have returned it. At 15' there is no breakup or background noise. The audio quality is far superior to what I had been using: an FM transmitter (common for car stereo setups) to a Sony Walkman am/fm radio on FM. While the latter setup works, there is a lot of background noise and cross/same channel interference because the Sony FM portable receives so many FM stations that there is always interference. Also, moving around (like rolling over), causes the signal to come and go on FM, hence my desire to try a Bluetooth solution)

This is where Bluetooth comes in. No interference whatsoever, No problem pairing this transmitter with the el cheapo Wally World Bluetooth receive adapter (which also works very, very well). I am taking the line level out of the DirecTV receiver and using the supplied adapter cable that came with the transmitter to get the audio from the sat receivre to the transmit adapter. I leave the transmit adapter plugged in all the time to the provided charging cable (a simple USB wall charger). On the receive side, the Wally World receive adapter is also powered all the time. Both devices appear to have an internal Li-ion battery, but they can both be left on charge power during normal use without risk to the batteries.

The transmit adapter is about 1\\" square and 1/8\\" thick, weighs next to nothing. The cheap Wally World receive adapter is very similar in size and weight, and it has the standard 1/8\\" (3.5 mm) stereo jack output)

If you want to duplicate this setup, keep in mind we are using \\"line level\\" audio, so there is no volume control. As it turns out, the audio level is perfect for night time listening with just a common setof \\"Frogz\\" ear buds. If I felt I needed volume control, I could find a set a ear buds with built in volume control, but so far, there is no need. The line levels are quiet enough to not \\"keep me awake\\", but certainly loud enough for clearly understandable dialog.

N.B. Concerning the \\"delay\\" referenced in other reviews: Using it on the DirecTV sat receiver, there is a perceptible delay, but it is very, very slight. If I look really hard to spot this \\"issue\\", I can see it now and then...and to be honest, that problem manifests all on its own from DirecTV without any bluetooth transmitter. Nevertheless, there is \\"some\\" delay, however slight, but not enough to confuse or even mildly annoy me. Further, I got it to \\"fall asleep\\" to, so most of the time I have the TV off when listening to this setup. I did make a point, however, of evaluating the delay carefully before writing this review. It is possible that each device may show differing delays, but I don't see the kind of delays that some have written about. Maybe I will in the future, but so far, there just isn't any issue. Maybe the pairing of this transmitter with the el cheapo Wally World receiver adapter is just a happy marriage. Who knows?

Highly recommended (both transmitter and receiver).
